ui.intro: Join the frames of a scene to reveal everything the camera travelled across. Explore the demo, then follow the same steps with your own GIF or video.

sections.title: Launch Framosik
p: On Windows x64, extract the entire ZIP and open {exe}. On Linux x86_64, extract the .tar.gz and run {bin} inside the Framosik folder. Keep {internal} next to the executable.
Choose {open} or press {ctrlO} and open {demoFile} from the package. The first frame shows the robot’s feet. The camera travels up the same illustration over 37 frames.

sections.title: Mark a single scene
p: In {original}, scrub the timeline or use {play} and the arrows to find both ends. Click {mark_start} and {mark_end}, or type the numbers into {first} and {last}. Both endpoints are included.
For the demo, use 1 through 37 and leave {step} at 1. In your own clip, stop before a cut or transition. A larger step processes fewer frames but leaves less shared detail for alignment.

sections.title: Choose alignment and blending
p: Under {movement}, pick {vertical} for the robot, {horizontal} for a sideways pan, or {free} for a diagonal pan. Use {zoom_motion} when the view moves closer or farther away with a uniform change in scale.
Under {mode}, {preserve} keeps existing linework. {feather} blends edges across the distance set by {feather_width}. {average} mixes shared pixels and can double outlines if the subject moves.

Start with {similarity} at 65% and {overlap} at 20%. The first sets how closely frames must match, the second how much area they must share. Use {crop} to remove a fixed subtitle strip from each frame, measured in source pixels.

sections.title: Watch the image grow
p: Click {stitch}. The {result} tab shows the growing image during processing. The log records confidence and displacement for each frame. Use {fit} for the whole scene or {zoom} to inspect individual pixels.

Scroll over the image to zoom and drag to pan. Over the options panel, the wheel scrolls through the controls. If you need to stop, {cancel} keeps the partial result. The full demo at 100% produces a 480 × 1080 px image.

sections.title: Finish and export
p: Once stitching ends, {finish} becomes available on the left. Inspect a seam at 100%. Start with a low {seam_soft} value to soften a line or use {seam_color} for a local colour difference. Click {apply_finish}.

Each application starts from the original mosaic. To compare, return both values to zero and apply again. {export} or {ctrlS} saves the last applied finish, with transparency in areas no frame covered. {report} writes a JSON file with settings, accepted and rejected frames, and the reason for an interruption.

sections.title: Make it your workspace
p: Open {view} to select the {theme} and {language}. {gradients} controls the glow. With gradients enabled, {animations} switches motion in the title and controls on or off. Preferences are saved automatically.
Open {about} to check the installed version or visit the website, repository and donation page. The language selector at the top of this guide works independently of the app.

faq: Stitching stopped at a particular frame. What can I do?

Check the last accepted frame, shorten the range and return the step to 1. For an isolated mismatch, {skip} tries subsequent frames against the last accepted one. Start a new mosaic after a true scene cut.
Why do I see stripes or double outlines in a zoom?

Try {zoom_motion} with closely spaced frames and {feather}. Inspect the seams, then apply a light finish. Rotation, perspective, parallax and animated layers can prevent one transform from aligning the entire scene.
I reached the size limit or my video will not open.
Lower {resolution} or split the range. {limit} caps the mosaic size in megapixels. Video support depends on the codec. If a file will not open, try an MP4 copy encoded with H.264.
